name: Dr. Jart Cicapair

lead: Cicapair is a product line from Dr. Jart+, a Seoul-based skincare brand, built around centella asiatica, known as tiger grass or cica. It is aimed at skin that looks red or irritated.

The appearance payoff is calmer, less visibly red skin. Centella as a plant has a long traditional use for minor wounds, though clinical efficacy has not been established in clinical research according to Wikipedia.

paras: People use it as a soothing step in a routine, such as creams, serums or color-correcting products designed to offset redness. It is often layered under sunscreen.
Topical centella can cause contact dermatitis and irritation in some people.[3] Patch-testing a new product is common practice.

angle.text: The line is marketed to reduce the look of redness and irritation, helping skin appear calmer and more even.

lead: Cicapair is a line from Dr. Jart+, a South Korean skincare brand founded in 2004 by Lee Jin-Wook with dermatologist Jung Sung-jae, and now part of the Estee Lauder Companies.[1] The brand's centella-based products use tiger grass (Centella asiatica) to calm redness and soothe irritation.[1]
Centella contains triterpenoids such as asiaticoside and madecassoside, and has been used traditionally for skin conditions and minor wounds.[2]

paras: Dr. Jart+ launched in December 2004 and entered the US through Sephora in 2011.[1]
The plant has traditional use for dermatological conditions and minor wounds, and its compounds include asiaticoside and madecassoside.[2] Contact dermatitis from topical use has been reported.[2]
